newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Burma on probation, says Singapore paper.
newsitem.headline: Burma on probation, says Singapore paper.

text.p: Burma's ruling generals, widely accused of human rights abuses, should consider themselves on probation when the country joins ASEAN next month, Singapore's pro-government Straits Times newspaper said on Tuesday.

It said in an editorial that ASEAN, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, would fulfill a dream at its Kuala Lumpur summit next month when Burma, Laos and Cambodia join to bring the region under one umbrella.
"But ASEAN is also about human decency," it said.
"The generals should be made to learn that it is not in their interest to let ASEAN down with actions that are beyond the pale," the editorial said.
"Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's admonition that the SLORC (State Law and Order Restoration Council) should not regard membership as a form of pardon can be the grouping's watchword.
"Myanmar (Burma) is on probation; nothing more, nothing less."
